utterances.text: No, I think there is nothing after the questions have been asked and answered. I think that is all. It is only meant for the proceedings here. It's not a personal matter. You're merely a witness in these proceedings and nothing more, so have no fears at all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My integrity has been affected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, it hasn't been. The proceedings are very clear. The re-examination was very clear. You were acquitted on this charge and that is the end of this matter and you remain a gentleman and a soldier. Thank you very much for your assistance. Thank you. You are discharged now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a request to make. Our next witness is ready, but as I have already told you, Dr. Hadzihuseinovic is an important witness. I didn't know how long the cross-examination of this witness would take. I have quite a large number of documents, so I would ask that I can begin with the examination after the break so that it could be done efficiently. If I may, I would be grateful, if not, I shall start, but I think it would be more expeditious if I were allowed to start the examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean asking him questions on what you indicated was your line of examination? Is that complicated? Asking questions about the municipal authority and the question about the coordinator and the like, do you think that that's complicated that you cannot start. You can start and then we will have the break and then you can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can start with the preliminaries, asking him his name, what his position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't think you have too many problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can start. The witness is waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In 20 minutes, you will have the break and you can arrange the rest. Please kindly invite the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I raise a matter in relation to this witness, Dr. Hadzihuseinovic. It was my intention to cross-examine this witness at the conclusion of his examination-in-chief. Unfortunately, I have a commitment, in another matter, in another chamber, and will involve me in that chamber tomorrow morning and on Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure Ms. Residovic cannot hear what my friend is saying because she must hear it through interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you said because I now have the headphones and I can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't realise that Ms. Residovic didn't have her headphones on. I'm just making an application for Your Honours indulgence in relation to this witness who it was my intention to cross-examine. I am committed to another matter tomorrow morning and Friday morning which, if this witness goes longer than today, would impact upon my ability to cross-examine him, which was what my intention was. Unfortunately, in the other matter, I need to be in that chamber at least tomorrow and the next day. I don't need to be there this afternoon, even though it's sitting, but I will need to be there on Thursday and Friday, in the mornings certainly. If this witness, Dr. Hadzihuseinovic has not completed his evidence by the end of today, then I'll be in difficulties in terms of cross-examining him if it was to continue tomorrow morning and my application, Your Honours, is to ask your indulgence to permit another witness to be deposed in the morning so that the cross-examination could take place in the afternoon, tomorrow afternoon, assuming his evidence in chief is completed today. If it's not, then evidence in chief continuing tomorrow afternoon and then Friday afternoon. I can indicate to Your Honours that based on what I know or anticipate his testimony to be, I would hope to complete my cross-examination certainly in an afternoon and hopefully in the space of a couple of hours. I would endeavour to do all I could to tailor any cross-examination to come within that time. I regret, Your Honours, that I have to do this but unfortunately, the scheduling of the cases is such that it has created this difficulty for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is very difficult for the Trial Chamber to reschedule any cases at all. He has been fixed to be deposed. The witness is here. I suppose -- so I don't know when it's necessary for you to cross-examine, read the transcripts and then do that, but definitely we have no intention of rescheduling any witness's testimony because it's more critical for us to continue as we have scheduled than any other Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that's my application, and if Your Honours are going to decline it, then fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We certainly would not accept it. We reject the application. Call your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I call Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we swear the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the name of God, the merciful, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may sit down. Take your seat. RUSMIR SAFET HADZIHUSEINOVIC

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. Will you please introduce yourself to the court and tell us your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Rusmir Safet Hadzihuseinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, before I proceed with questions, I should like to warn you, like I have done with all our witnesses, of a technical matter, namely, both of us speak the same language, and it would be easy for us to -- for me to ask the questions and for you to answer them immediately. But as every word we say has to be interpreted and has to go down in the transcript and be understood by everyone in this courtroom, the Trial Chamber in the first place, I would like to ask you to listen to the interpretation on the set of headphones on the table. You will hear the end of the interpretation. You can turn on the volume and when you no longer hear the interpretation, only then answer my question, please. In that way, everyone in the courtroom will be able to follow. Have you understood these instructions, Dr. Hadzihuseinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I understand fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Dr. Hadzihuseinovic, will you tell me, please, when and where you were born, what is your ethnic origin and your citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on the 23rd of May, 1947 in Konjic. My citizenship is Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, what schools have you graduated from and what is your profession and what is your speciality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I graduated from secondary school in Konjic, the school of medicine in Belgrade and I specialised in urology in Niche and Belgrade, so my speciality is urology.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you served in the former JNA, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where have you worked as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My first employment was in Konjic and after that I also worked in Serbia for about seven years and I spent some time working abroad too. From 1986, I have been working permanently in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Hadzihuseinovic, did you become politically active in the period before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a political activist, did you participate as a candidate at any elections, and if so which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as a candidate of the party of democratic action, SDA, at the first multi-party and democratic elections held in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your political function in the SDA at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I held the position of president of the SDA for Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell the court, very briefly, who won at the elections and how the authorities were structured after those elections and how the government was established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I shall be very brief. The SDA party won and in the newly established municipal assembly of Konjic, which consisted of 60 deputies, the SDA had 28 seats, the HDZ 14, the Serb democratic party, the SDS 9, and all the other parties 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What position were you assigned to after the elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the elections, by decision of the municipal assembly of Konjic, that is all the deputies in the assembly, I was democratically elected president of the municipal assembly of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that at the time you discharged the functions you have described, will you tell us, did Zejnil Delalic participate in those Parliamentary elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as far as I know because he was abroad at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After those elections in 1990, was Zejnil Delalic elected to any state bodies in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later on in 1992, was Zejnil Delalic nominated or elected as a member of any state organ in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As president of the SDA party for Konjic municipality, do you know whether Zejnil Delalic was a member of the SDA of Konjic or the SDA of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the party of democratic action of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because the SDA party of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have its branches abroad. That was not legally possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zejnil Delalic, in 1992, was a member of any other political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Zejnil Delalic perform any political function in 1992, in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Zejnil Delalic, during the first multi-party elections, assist those elections and assist the elected authorities in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Delalic supported, financially, the new democratic forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, only financially.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he make a gift to the municipal assembly of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can recall, a jeep was bought for the needs of the municipal assembly of Konjic. I think also a typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in view of these answers by the witness, I should like to show the witness a number of documents contained in the supporting material of the expert witness, so could I please have five minutes to get those documents, as I have not prepared them yet, or may I do that after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and assemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may continue, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind the witness he's under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, good afternoon, I hope you were able to take some rest. I would now like to the registrar to help me show the Prosecutors Exhibit No. 99/7 -- 2. I have copies, so that we can facilitate a communication here. Here are the copies, which can be provided for both the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution. Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, would you please review these documents. Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I have never seen this document before. I see it for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the president of SDA in Konjic in 1992, can you tell me whether this document represents, a copy of a membership card, of an SDA member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document does not represent a membership card of a SDA member -- a Bosnia SDA member.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, can the document please be returned to the registrar. With the usher's assistance, I would now like to show the witness a document from D-136. This will be from the supporting material of the expert witness report and this would be in D-35. I have sufficient copies for both the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution. Again, just to facilitate the matters. Sir, I believe that you can see that this document was produced in Vienna, so I am not going to ask you to testify to its authenticity, but I would like you to read the body of text, of the certificate. Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, do you know that in Vienna there was an association of the Muslim/Bosnian culture circle which was active at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of its activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, this document can also be returned now. Now I would like to request that the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Even if it is held that he is a member of SDA, how it connects him with the Celebici camp? Let's confine ourselves to the role played by Mr. Zenu (phoen) in the war presidency, if there was any, his associations with the Celebici camp, if any. We're concerned with the Celebici camp, we're not concerned with his other activities at all. The membership of the SDA will not necessarily mean that he has involvement in the setting up of the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Whether his membership creates an offence, I don't know. Whether that he's a member of that organisation makes any difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, you should ask this question of the Prosecution because they offered it into evidence. They said that they found it in the Vienna documents and that they had asked someone and that it proves the position of superiority. All I want to find out from this witness is whether this was a fact or not. So this is the evidence that were already produced before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, definitely it leads to nowhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You asked him about his role in the war presidency, if there was any. His connections in the Celebici camp, if there was any. These are the questions relevant for us. Membership of SDA is really irrelevant in this regard. I may be a member of SDA, but still I have nothing to do with Celebici. I may not be a member of the SDA, I may still have a role to play in that. So let's confine ourselves to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am very glad that this is your thinking, but since the Prosecution has produced the documents that I am referring to now, will you please allow me to ask that through this witness, about these documents. But this is the part of the backbone of this allegation, of the Prosecution's allegation that this authenticates his responsibility, his superiority. And now I would like to ask for another document. It is in D-34 and it is Exhibit No. 136. And again, I have enough copies for the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, I am not going to ask you to authenticate this document, however, if you had read its contents, since you've already answered part of my questions, regarding the contents, can you just tell the Court whether the contents of these documents is truthful, with regard to your personal knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, the contents of these documents are fully truthful in full measure of its contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since this witness has confirmed the authenticity of this document with respect to the events that it covers in 1992 and on the basis of its relevance, I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: To say that he has read a letter saying certain things. That's what he's just done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the break, I have asked all these questions of the witness, whether he was a member of the SDA, whether the jeep was purchased with it. And now he has reviewed the letter and he has confirmed it. He says that they pertain to the events from 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's not his letter, he didn't write it, is it? He didn't write this letter?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is confirming its truthfulness and I believe that this is relevant and so on the basis of its relevance, I am tendering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How does it relate? His evidence is sufficient to what he must have said about Delalic and his membership. For him now to say that this is own evidence, a letter which you are now trying to tender through him, it's a letter -- he couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hope that you will apply the same standard for some other additional evidence that may be turned in because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have told you, he's not the right person to tender this letter. And don't say I am applying a different standard. If you do not understand the procedure, you say so. I have not said anything different than that he cannot tender this letter. He's not the author. And there's no way he could authenticate it. And then you say, one is applying a different standard. That's all you've been referring in all you've been saying and I don't like it. I never apply different standards. I have no personal interest in any of these things. It's only professional responsibility, I am just charging you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my professional ethics, I have full respect for the Trial Chamber, but I would also request that my professionalism is not brought up in open court here. I am just going to go on with my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber, when we express an opinion about you tendering any particular document, if it's not this particular witness who should tender it, I'll say so. If it's right for him to do so, obviously it will be admitted but definitely this is not his letter. It was not written by him and he agrees with the contents, it does not make it his own document, so he cannot tender it. In any event, I don't see the need for it, for entering it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is my place to offer documents into evidence and it is for you to accept them or not. For instance, the SDA membership card was admitted and I believe that I was following the procedures, which has been established in the practice of this Trial Chamber. If I have made a mistake, I can go correct myself, but I was hoping that I have been doing it, the right thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Admitted, who is tendering it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, could you please tell me whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic, at the time when you were president of the war presidency, was a member of any state of body or did he have any political function in the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that I will be repeating an answer which I have given previously. Mr. Delalic was not a member of any state body or any political body in the Konjic municipality, during my tenure, while I was the leader there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just one thing, just for clarification, we're just concerned with 1992, he was not a member of any party, he was not a member of your particular party in 1992, just to bring in the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I request that the witness be shown document D-136, D-31. And again, I have provided a sufficient number of copies for everyone. Were you able to read through the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I am not going to seek here, the authentication of this document, because other persons have authenticated it at the defence request in '96. But I want to tell you whether this document reflects the position of Mr. Zejnil Delalic with respect to his functions in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely this document reflects that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Now don't you think it's better if you ask him, whether this witness was a member of the body at that time, and whether he knew Delalic was a member or so, of the body. If he says so, I think his evidence will be as strong as you can get. You have put him forward as the president of the municipal council and he's -- for the period and why should he be able to give evidence of that period?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I introduced this witness as the president and I also offered you a document which speaks of Zejnil. He could confirm this because he was the SDA president in Konjic. He was also the president of the municipal assembly and president of war presidency. So, he personally knows this fact. This is why have been offering both this document and the previous document because it confirms the truthfulness. I did not ask him this in 1992. I received a document in 1996 from different bodies, but this person knows about the truthfulness of these facts as of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Suspicion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- As you can get. He was president of the body and he can give evidence of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but the Prosecution cast out, as to the truthfulness of this document, that appeared in the expert witness report. So, what I am trying to do here is to talk about, is truthfulness, because the truthfulness of it has been brought into doubt by the Prosecution and this is why I am trying to have this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's here, I don't see all this argument. The witness is present, in person, to finish whatever cross-examination arising out of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, am I understanding you correctly, that you are not admitting this document offered by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the Judge Karibi-Whyte please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to ask you something. I would not like to go on discussing this document. I was provided a videotape of the shelling of Konjic by this witness and a copy of it has been made available for the Prosecution. If you believe that this is an indisputable fact and if the Prosecution is also not disputing it, I have no need to show this videotape. It is also going to talk about the circumstances under which the coordinator was appointed, but if this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are you disputing that Konjic was shelled frequently during 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COWLES
utterances.text: We don't know how frequently it was shelled, but we don't dispute that it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This has been said several times, these are not issues in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, in the light of this discussion, I am just going to ask you without showing the videotape, I am going to ask you as mayor of this town, when did the shelling of Konjic begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Konjic started being shelled in the month of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How often was Konjic shelled in this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first shelling started on 4 May, 1992 and continued tenaciously on a daily basis. It happened that this town, which was very small, up to 500 shells would fall. It was -- those were horror days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On 6 April, you were appointed the president of the municipal assembly, of this town. Can you tell me now, apart from the JNA, which at that time was in the barracks, was there any other structure that was -- organisation that was supposed to defend the country and town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the members of the Yugoslav People's Army, who were in military facility, the only structures that existed within the system of the legal and legitimate defence of the town were members of the ministry of the interior. That is the police and members of the Territorial Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though Bosnia and Herzegovina became an independent state, do you know whether the JNA tried, forcibly, to mobilise people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that, namely, let me inform Your Honours with a date which is very significant and which impacts my answer to this question. Actually, the general staff of the armed forces of the former Yugoslavia, by its order from 1990, required that all the arms of the Territorial Defence should be placed in the warehouses of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, this is a fact that the court has been informed about several times. Will you please tell us what is important in connection with this fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is important is that the Yugoslav People's Army tried to carry out mobilisation itself, illegally, by trying to illegally seize the documents on mobilisation held in the national defence secretariat of Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, as a legal authority in Konjic, when the war began on April the 6th, did you follow developments in Bosnia-Herzegovina and did you react to those developments? If you did, tell us how.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, I did. As representatives of the legal authorities and the bodies we presided over, we undertook all the necessary steps which would serve the interests of the defence of the city. Let me give you a number of examples. It was our duty to secure the most important facilities in the town itself such as the central electricity power station, the water supply system, to ensure supervision over economic facilities and supervision over all other crucial facilities according to instructions of the state authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did all the parties that participated and won at the elections, adopt the same attitude towards the legitimacy of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not. That is not correct. The Serb Democratic Party of the municipality of Konjic, was carrying out instructions from the Serb Democratic Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, accordingly, it boycotted the referendum, on the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and after that, it took a series of steps and measures which, from the standpoint of the legal authorities, constituted a rebellion and non-respect for the authority of the state they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the president of the assembly, did you convene the assembly for it to take decisions in accordance with measures taken by the state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Pursuant to decisions of the competent state bodies, passed in the first half of the month of April, because Bosnia-Herzegovina was an internationally recognised state, I convened the municipal assembly of Konjic, on the 17th of April, at which the appropriate conclusions and decisions were adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of this position that you took regarding the defence of the city, were there threats that the town would be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. General Kukanjac, who was the commander of the second military district in Sarajevo, personally by telephone, threatened me, saying that Konjic would be raised to the ground and he did so on several occasions. And we were just doing our job as the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that connection, did you address the inhabitants over Radio Konjic and was that recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In order to keep the public informed, I acted in a positive direction on a number of occasions, and certainly those recordings must still exist on tapes, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, since you were the legal authorities, elected legally, do you know whether at the beginning of '92 there were any illegal groups that were preparing the defence of the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In answer to that question, I would say the following: There was no need for us, on our side, to form any illegal groups because we had a system and regular institutions functioning within that system. We had members of the ministry of internal affairs and members of the Territorial Defence. The only forces illegal and paramilitary forces, the only illegal and paramilitary forces were those of the Serb Democratic Party which would not accept the legal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, in view of what you have just said and regardless of what was happening in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, tell me, please, whether in 1992 were there any Green Berets, the Patriotic League as armed formations and others like them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, such armed formations did not exist in Konjic. As for the Green Berets, I know that such a social organisation, a non-political organisation, therefore, was formed in Konjic in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to your personal knowledge, could anyone, including Zejnil Delalic, in 1992 be a member of any such organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, what did you undertake, in concrete terms, to take over military facilities and place them under the competence of the legal authorities or, more specifically, what did the municipal assembly, at its meeting on the 17th, do with regard to the degrees and instructions received from the state bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 6th of April as an international legal entity, by decision of the competent state bodies, and that means the presidency of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well as the ministry of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was our duty to act pursuant to those instructions and decisions. At the mentioned assembly meeting on the 17th of April, 1992 attended by representatives of all the political parties, the agenda was reviewed and that agenda had to do with the political and security situation in the municipality of Konjic, and the report on the same was submitted by the chief of the police station, Mr. Jasmin Guska. One of the agenda items also was the structuring of the Territorial Defence and the proposal on the appointment of the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic because the previous man's term of office had expired.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, exactly on what date was that assembly meeting held, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was held on the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was attending that meeting in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have just said, the composition of members was the usual one. It was attended by deputies of the SDA, HDZ, SDS and other political parties that had a share in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall who chaired that assembly meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not a question of remembering. I was the president and I chaired the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was Zejnil Delalic a member of the assembly at the time and did he, at all, attend the assembly meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely out of the question. Zejnil Delalic could not have been a member of the assembly because he was not a deputy, nor did he participate in the elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was proposed, at that assembly meeting, as the new commander of the reorganised Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Enver Regepovic (phoen) was proposed as the new commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your proposal also mean that Enver Regepovic was, indeed, elected commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. Our right was merely to nominate candidates, and the actual appointment was done by the republican staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I now ask the witness to be shown -- first, may it be marked for identification and then shown to the witness, that is the minutes of this assembly meeting? I have a sufficient number of copies for everyone. This is the original minutes with the translation and here are the copies for their Honours and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document number 173/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, will you please look at the signature at the end of the minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the signature of the secretary, Mr. Muhamed Djikic, secretary of the municipal assembly who is still working in the municipality but holds a different position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, can you tell me, is that the minutes of that meeting? Did you have those minutes in your hands in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, and these are the minutes of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that these minutes reflect the procedure of the transformation of the Territorial Defence and the nomination of the new commander and this witness presided over that meeting, I tender these minutes into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can tender it through this witness, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask, since I have received from the witness, a videotape of that meeting, I should like to show just the beginning of that tape because I should like to tender that tape into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can carry on with your direct evidence. It is not necessary. We don't need the tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me the number of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D173/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, you said that all parties attended this assembly meeting. Who was the Vice-President of the assembly at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the president of the Serb Democratic Party, Mr. Dulo Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he too participate in the work of this assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did and he was a member of the working presidency of the assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting ended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the meeting, the competent state bodies started working on the implementation of the decisions and conclusions adopted by that assembly meeting; however, the Serb democratic party and its representatives in the government refused to support those decisions and actually, they actually sided with the other party, namely --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That will be sufficient. Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, the fact that the Serbs abandoned the legitimate bodies and that the town was being shelled, did that mean that conditions existed according to the law and your statute, that a different method of operation should be adopted in accordance with the constitution and the law or, to be more specific, could the assembly continue to meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the last meeting of the assembly, in that form, and pursuant to the regulations in force, as well as the statute of the municipal assembly of Konjic, which stipulated that under conditions of an immediate threat of war or the proclamation of the state of war, the assembly should interrupt its work and all its competencies should be taken over by the presidency of the municipal assembly, the composition of which is defined by the statute of the municipal assembly and which was known at the time as the war presidency because there was a war so that is how people called it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a body that was envisaged by the regulations that existed in peace time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you, in Konjic, adopt that statute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, that was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should now like, with the assistance of the usher, to show the witness the statute of the municipal assembly with translations of the relevant portions relating to procedures in case of war to see whether the witness can recognise this statute as the document he has just been referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D174/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the end, the provisions that are relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me first ask the witness whether this document, that you are looking at, is the statute of the municipality of Konjic, in effect, on the 6th of April, 1992 when the war began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so. That was the statute in force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I tender it into evidence as a Defence Exhibit .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You have not translated the whole document. I'm interested in the provision relating to the composition of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have here the competencies, article 68, the competencies are transferred to the presidency. Article 66 talks about the competencies of the assembly and which documents it is authorised to adopt and later on the law regulates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is a document, a very lengthy one, in Bosnian language. The translation is only about three pages. I was just wondering the provision relating to composition of the war presidency, if there is any such provision, who would compose the war presidency or was it not part of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is something about it in article 68. We can look through it again and, if necessary, have translated all the relevant provisions. We thought that we had done so. Those articles of relevance for this case, because article 66 and 67 refer to that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: See, I just wanted to check up whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic could ever be, under the constitution, a member of the war presidency. That's all. I was just wondering if there was any provision in these regulations with regard to the persons who would constitute that body. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me read to you article 68. It says the composition of the presidency of the municipal assembly is determined by special decisions of the municipal assembly in accordance with the law, and we already have the law in the evidence which specifies who enters ex officio and who is elected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Where the assembly could not meet. If the assembly could not meet, who would determine the composition of the presidency. This is what I was wondering. Because if the assembly was there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I answer that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'd be glad to do that. I think I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When the assembly could not meet, so then who would determine who would be a member of the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was established by existing regulations from before and members of the war presidency were there ex officio, that is the president of the municipal assembly, the president -- no, it isn't stated here because it says that it is determined by other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Which says who will be the members of the war presidency, but I'm thinking of April 1993 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not correct. In the situation before the war, we had regulations that stipulated who composed the war presidency in the case of an immediate threat of war and a state of war, so allow me to tell you who they are. Ex officio, the president of the municipal assembly is the president of the war presidency. The president of the executive council of the municipal assembly is a member of the war presidency. The chief of the public security station is a member of the war presidency. The commander of civil defence is a member of the war presidency. The presidents of the clubs of parties, that is of political parties, are also ex officio members of the presidency. That would be the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this statute, given the relevance of some of its provisions but also because the president of the municipality has recognised it as its own document, I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You could tender it but it's quite inadequate. Much of it is of not much assistance. It is written in a language which is not one of the languages of the Tribunal. Only article 66, 67, 68 and 69 and 70 and they are the.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: From your Defence point of view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So it can hardly be of any use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We now know what the composition of the war presidency is from the mouth of the president so how will this help in resolving the questions before us? So don't waste time and money in getting the whole thing translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, what are you trying to show by tendering it? What does it support, because if it supports the question of convening the war presidency, we might sufficiently rely on the evidence of the witness? But if there are other things you want to introduce here, it might not be of any help. The document you want to introduce might not be of any assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is also the article 66 here, which is important, because it speaks of the kind of documents, decisions which the war presidency could adopt and also you have a whole range of documents which have been tendered, introduced, and now we are trying to provide the basis on which these were introduced. However, if you are asking me to tender just an abridged version of the statute, and, indeed, as you said, it could be a waste of money and maybe court's time to have the whole thing translated, I'm also willing to introduce just those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Article 66 does not talk about presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It speaks of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: From April to November when Zejnil Delalic was in Konjic. Before that, he was not even there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The only against you is the Prosecution. They are not challenging the activities of the municipal council, are they? Nobody is attacking it. Nobody denies its legitimacy, so I don't know what you are really about. Perhaps the Prosecutor might assist us here, if you have anything against the municipal council as a legitimate body? I don't see all the arguments now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Zejnil Delalic was outside Bosnia before April. He comes in April to attend some funeral. He stays on to November because of the situation in Bosnia, and the war presidency was constituted. Article 66 does not talk about the competencies of the war presidency so what's the use of having it on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this article directly speaks to the activities of the war presidency. Let me explain. The war presidency, in practical terms, substitutes for the assembly. It replaces it so article 66 speaks about the competencies of both the assembly and the war presidency because the war presidency is a body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I understand that and we have heard enough of that. Is it possibly what you have in mind is the assembly passed a resolution appointing someone that -- probably what you have in mind is that the assembly passed a resolution appointing someone as a commander of the TO. Well, in the minutes, we'll find the objection of the SDS representative in the assembly that this can only be done by the republican TO. Have you noticed that in the minutes of the assembly? It says, the subject before the assembly is appointment of a commander of the TO and it says the SD representative, I can't pronounce his name, emphasise that such decision could be made only conditionally and the consent was to be given by the Republic's view of the TO and the suggestion was taken into account. Even at that time, the SDS representative brought, before the assembly, the correct legal position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was not a member of the SDS. This was a member of the social democratic party. He was of Serb ethnic background, but the assembly did accept his proposal according to the law and only later when the republican body did what it did. However, I offered the videotape and this here is the person sitting in front of you who actually accepted that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You exercised the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the social democratic party, not the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't see any problem. If you have any evidence to lead, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one comment, I think it's relevant, Your Honours, because as of 17 April, the assembly is not competent in appointing commanders of Territorial Defence which can also be seen from the videotape which we have not seen, and this is what the witness has been saying, which is completely opposite of what the Prosecution has been saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Read the indictment again and try to know exactly what is the accusation against your client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Even if you assume that the war presidency, the assembly were competent to appoint the commander of the TO, but is there any evidence that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed as commander of the TO? We're only concerned with your client.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly what we're trying to prove, that it never happened. However, the Prosecution claims the opposite of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, given the situation and the intense shelling of the town, how was the town supplied from the end of April until the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation in Konjic was very difficult. In all spheres of daily lives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- we've had some evidence on that, that people were eating plums.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To make a long story short, we were deficient in everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how many refugees arrived in the Town of Konjic from different parts of Bosnia and who took care of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first refugees started arriving in Konjic in the month of March, that is in late March and early April. From the villages, which -- from the villages from which the Serb paramilitary units had driven out non-Serb population. These were the villages of Jakici, Racaci (phoen) --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, can you tell us the approximate figure of the refugees at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total number of refugees in Konjic, in that period, was somewhere around 15,000. These were the refugees from Eastern Herzegovina, Eastern Bosnia, who, who had walked for days across mountains and had great difficulties in reaching safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, as a legal authority in Konjic, did you place under control, certain military objects, facilities in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, let me re-emphasise the date of independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The international community recognised this country and from that day on, all property was -- all this property belonged to the legal government authorities. Following the instructions of the competent state bodies, on the nights between 18 and 19 April 1992, we took control of the facilities for production of ordnance, that was the Igman Company. After that, we took control of the compound of the Celebici barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, do you know how the Celebici barracks were taken over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Commander of the Celebici barracks was a Bosniac, I believe that he was a warrant officer in the former JNA and his name was Narcis Hasacic. He signed off on loyalty to the legal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally involved in the negotiations about -- on the take over of the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion in a hospital where I was working, because even though I was a president of the municipality, I still worked in the hospital two days a week and on one occasion this person came to me. I had never seen him before. He was in civilian clothes. He introduced himself to me and he expressed his wish, as a Bosniac, to turn over the Celebici barracks to us. Since I had previously received information on this wish of his, I informed the competent persons in the TO headquarters and the entire procedure, the entire operation was then conducted by the TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, do you know whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic took part in the take-over of this facility. And do you know in what capacity and was he at all involved in a take-over of the barracks by the legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already stated that this take-over was conducted through the Territorial Defence headquarters and the -- and Delalic's involvement in it may have been only in transportation of the material found there because Mr. Zejnil Delalic had absolutely no role in the TO headquarters or in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, as a physician, can you tell us whether your health centre was prepared for such sudden onslaught of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given the size of the Konjic town, before the war we did not have enough hospital facilities. We only had some specialised units. And given the large influx of the wounded and other persons who were flowing into Konjic and because of the fact that the roads had been blocked both in the direction of Sarajevo and Mostar, we resorted to establishing a war hospital in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How was your hospital equipped with medical supplies and other equipment at that time? Was it adequate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why are you objecting to asking him how the hospital was equipped?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Because it's irrelevant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Probably what you want to share is, there were not enough facilities for the detention of persons, so they had to move to Celebici. That's what the witness has said. The witness has said yes in Konjic and the number of persons who had been arrested or detained was much larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is a hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's about influx of so many people into Konjic community, the increase of refugees into the place. The need for this type of facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I won't argue any further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can ask him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a lack of medication, especially things needed for surgery because that was the greatest need. We needed most of those supplies, because we had a lot of very serious and bad wounds coming from the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given how you described the situation in Konjic, the blockade and everything, do you know as a president of the municipality, that the Konjic authorities have adopted certain decisions and taken steps to lift this blockade off Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will gladly answer this question. But before that, I would like to give a brief introduction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it's better you answer the question, instead of getting in on your own case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The competent military authorities, which means the TO headquarters and also the competent police authorities, given the fact that the Serb paramilitary formations had blocked the town from the north, it was in the Village of Bradina on the M-17 highway and on the south-west. It was a regional road at the village called Donje Selo or lower village. And thereby, a large area of the Konjic municipality was effectively blockaded, blocked, and this is where some 16,000 people live and this is an area called Neretvica. On the other side, Serb forces from the area of Borci, which had occupied this area as early as 1991, while preparing the operation Dubrovnik, so the Town of Konjic was surrounded, on all sides, by some kind of a ring.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, you explained how the situation was, but as a member of the municipal government and as a physician, do you know whether, during the combat operations around Donje Selo and Bradina, there were any casualties, either dead or wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very, very vividly this period at Donje Selo. During the lifting of the blockade, two members of the police force were killed. If necessary I can even state their names Mustafa Boric and Velija Niksic. And at Bradina, a 16-year-old boy was killed by the name of Rizvanovic, and a member of the HVO was also killed. I believe his first named was Goran. And I know this because I attended the funerals of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a physician, do you know whether there were any wounded during this fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. There were a number of wounded and some of them have consequences of these injuries to date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, can you tell us whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic, that is in May, 1992, was in Konjic and, according to your knowledge, did he take part in any of these operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic at that time was not in Konjic. I believe that he went on official duty in the sense of procurement of certain material, that is logistics equipment. He went to Croatia. And, as far as I recall, he did not attend the funerals of these men either. Because this is a custom in our area, in our -- that everybody attends funerals.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, given this complex situation in town, the shelling, the lack of goods, dead and wounded, did there come a time when the military headquarters and the war presidency were to assess the situation and agree as to how to proceed in these war -- in this wartime situation, advanced wartime situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can answer this question in the affirmative. We were sitting continuously because we just had too much work to do, at every moment in time, and we also did not know whether we would survive the day. And I recall this was in the later part of May or, more specific, I think this was 18 May, 1992, the war presidency of the Konjic Municipality held a meeting with the joint command of the armed forces of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next line of questioning is a block of questions, I am wondering whether if this would be a good moment to break off before entering this area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will now rise and resume at 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, where are we? You were continuing with your --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was a slight lack of clarity in connection with the question put by Judge Jan. To clarify this fact, I should like to give to the witness once again the minutes of the 9th meeting of the municipal assembly in order to be able to ask him two brief questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with the command responsibility of your client. Even if there is no clarity, it doesn't affect it at all. It's nobody's case that he was appointed as the TO commander by the war presidency, so we are not concerned whether the war presidency appointed someone as commander of the TO. It doesn't relate to your client at all so why go into that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have they conflicting duties? Are there any conflicting duties between the coordinator and the TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What was his function of the coordinator if he was appointed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him us tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is more important than going into these matters about the competency of the war presidency and all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand you very well, but as the president observed, I understand the indictment very well and the position of the Prosecution. This document and this session was very important whether the assembly could give him any kind of superior authority. That is where the story of the Prosecution begins. And the position of the Defence, you drew attention to a point which I wish to elucidate with the help of this witness, the beginning of the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The issue before us is the command responsibility of your client, nothing more than that. Admittedly, he was a coordinator appointed by the war presidency. Ask him what were the functions assigned to him and did it really relate to the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you remember, there are two significant issues about Delalic. He was appointed coordinator. He was also appointed Tactical Group 1 commander. He must have acted in these two areas. If his activities in doing these two areas that has brought him any of these offences for which he has been charged, so these are the only things that concern you, not whether any other thing happened somewhere. That has nothing to do with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't wish to go outside that framework, it may appear to be that, but my questions are leading to that crucial issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Then come to them straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to Judge Karibi-Whyte, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The minutes of the municipal assembly, these minutes are not a point to what has been disputed so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm sure as president of the war presidency, he has done lots of things and he can keep on telling us this for a year, but let us confine ourselves to those points which are in issue before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, at the assembly meeting that we have referred to, the former staff commander, Major Prevljak, did he inform the assembly on changes in the Territorial Defence and did you, accordingly, agree on a proposal for the new organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can answer that question in the positive, in the affirmative. Mr. Smajo Prevljak spoke at that meeting and informed us that that morning such a document had reached the staff headquarters from Sarajevo, a document that came from the republican staff of the Territorial Defence. He informed the assembly meeting of the same. At the same time, he informed the meeting that in the course of the meeting he expected confirmation from Sarajevo of our proposal on the appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, is it true then -- first, my question is: Did confirmation of your proposal arrive from Sarajevo on that day or the next day; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, it didn't reach us in the course of our meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your proposals were endorsed by the republican authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. I do know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That leads to the appointment of one -- please be concerned with Mr. Delalic. Please confine yourself to Mr. Delalic's role in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My next question, Your Honours, from that day on, did all the legal authorities function in accordance with the new regulations. That is my question. The position of the Prosecution is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that day on, after approval came from the republican bodies, all the bodies acted in line with the any regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, you said that you had a joint meeting between the war presidency and the joint staff on the 18th of May. At that meeting, did you adopt any conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At that meeting, we did adopt conclusions. I said earlier on that that meeting was held and a series of conclusions were adopted at that meeting having to do with the civilian authorities and also a certain number of conclusions related to the bodies of the joint staff or, rather, the joint command of the armed forces. After that, all of us worked in accordance with our competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I should like to show the witness the text of the conclusions, which has already been admitted into evidence, for me to be able to ask a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document D175/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, have you looked at this text?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, whether after this meeting it was quite clear what were the competencies of the war presidency and what were the obligations and responsibilities of the command of the armed forces, of the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was completely clear. The war presidency had its own competencies according to the constitution, and the same applies to the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that these conclusions established that all the bodies had to act in accordance with their competencies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this joint meeting, did you, in the war presidency, review the implementation of the conclusions relating to you and the adoption of the corresponding decisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, on that day, reviewing your obligations and responsibilities, decide on the appointment of Zejnil Delalic to any particular assignment or position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did adopt such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this is a decision dated 18th of May, I should like to have this decision on the appointment of the coordinator. It is already in evidence, D136, D/11, also a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before asking you a question related to this decision, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, I want to ask you whether, in accordance with the new regulations, the war presidency could appoint the commander of the TO staff or other persons holding military positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency, according to the new regulations, absolutely could not appoint anyone to any military post because it didn't have any such authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have seen the decision that I have just given to you. Tell me, please, who signed this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my signature. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a decision whereby the war presidency appointed Zejnil Delalic the coordinator for the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is that decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, did this appointment mean an appointment of Zejnil Delalic to any kind of military position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not because, as I have already said, the war presidency is a civilian body so it could not make decisions on the appointment of any military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Zejnil Delalic in discharging the task that you assigned to him, could he issue orders to military structures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic absolutely could not issue any kind of orders to military structures because he was a civilian. As a civilian, this body in line with its constitutional and legal authority and in accordance with the statute of Konjic municipality appointed him as a civilian and in the status of a civilian to this position. As the body appointing him did not have those rights, then Mr. Delalic could not have had any such rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for a moment, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, in view of the fact that my learned colleague has checked that the conclusions dated 18th of May signed by this witness were not admitted as Defence exhibit. I'm now tendering them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You want them to be in evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to Judge Karibi-White, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You want the conclusions of --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of the 18th of May to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's admitted. The chairman himself said -- the chairman being here himself is sufficient. You don't need it for any purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, in point 2 of the decision on the appointment of Mr. Delalic, it is stated that he will directly coordinate work between the defence forces of Konjic municipality and the war presidency. Could you please tell us, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, what were in practise the duties of the coordinator appointed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The very word "coordinator" means that his duty was to reflect certain needs which certain bodies addressed to the war presidency or certain organs of the war presidency or the war presidency itself had certain requests in relation to the armed forces. I could give you some practical examples of those activities, if that is important for the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I or the court asks you about that, let me first ask whether you whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic attended the meeting of the war presidency when you appointed him to this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should like to remind their Honours what I have been saying. I said that Mr. Delalic was away, was in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's easy for you to answer. Was he at the meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not attend the meeting. He did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, in the period before he went to Croatia and while he was in Croatia as a civilian, as you said, what were the kinds of duties that he carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, before being appointed to this position of coordinator, engaged in similar activities. That is, he was working on logistic tasks. That is the procurement of material and technical means which were important for defence, for the defence of the Town of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, can you recall how it came about that Mr. Zejnil Delalic should have been appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wish to assure their Honours that his appointment in nothing special because such appointments to the position of co-ordinators were several. Therefore, the war presidency, which engaged in a large range of activities and which was very busy, would seek out ways to ensure maximum efficiency. And the idea to appoint him at the time was not actually, especially designed for him. The idea emerged that we should appoint a person who would be effective as a kind of mediator in dealing with certain problems between the civilian body, that is the war presidency and the joint command, that is the armed forces. The recommendation that he, himself, should be appointed came from the economic staff. Because Mr. Delalic was a well-known figure. He was known as a person who had been working for a number of years in business in economic affairs. And in the view of the economic staff, he was the most suitable person to discharge such a function. In view of his experience and the numerous connections he had both in the country and abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, a moment ago in answer the a question from His Honour Judge Jan, you explained the composition of the were presidency, to be even more precise, can you tell the Court whether in those days, the commander of the municipal staff or the commander of the joint staff, were they members of the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The commander of the municipal staff, or the commander of the joint command, was not a member of a war presidency that is certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, you also said that the situation was complicated and you wanted to simplify it, can you explain why some problems could not be resolved within the joint command and, in fact, what was your intention by appointing the commander, not the commander, the coordinator -- counsel, yes, I'm sorry -- what were the things that he was meant to take care of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will briefly explain that to the Court with the an aim behind the appointment of a coordinator. In view of the fact that there was a state of war, the war presidency was contacted by a series of persons every day from the armed forces and it is well known that the armed forces consisted of three bodies, three formations: members of the ministry of the interior, the HVO and the Territorial Defence. All three elements had their own separate command structure, the chain of command structure, chain of command, so that the civilian bodies would lose or waste a lot of time if they were to discuss the same things with each one of them. By appointing a coordinator as a civilian, as a person who would voice all those needs and communicate them between the war presidency and the armed forces. By doing this, in my view, the war presidency ensured greater efficiency of its work when it came to a large number of tasks that it had to discharge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, you just answered my follow up question, which was, did a coordinator actually facilitate your work with different formations that composed defence forces in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in this position, Mr. Zejnil Delalic could not issue orders, could Mr. Zejnil Delalic reach, himself, certain decisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, he absolutely could not take any decisions or issue any orders. His function was purely technical in nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
